title: Sworn to Secrets, Bound for Chult
summary: I have watched many a company assembled in the House of Healing, yet few so unlikely as this one. Vex, who assured all present that he was the only soul of good breeding in the room, came chiefly to outshine his cousin, while Grieg and Urida answered Azlund's postings in earnest and the goblin Chumble Crudluck answered chiefly the summons of a fruit bowl, from which a purloined banana found its way with impish precision into the seat of Vex's fine trousers just before he sat. They arrived in good time to catch Vander and Skamos holding a rapt crowd with tales of frost giants at Bryn Shander, of Artus Cimber, of the lost Harshnag and Hekaton, and the fall of Imyrith. Then Azlund, warmed near to tears by his cousin's arrival and much to Vex's private disgust, drew them upstairs and laid bare the great matter, the Death Curse that lets no dead soul rest, the Soulmonger at its root, and the long road south to Chult. For a modest purse apiece, a map of that green and hungry land, and the promise of far richer reward should they return victorious, the company took the charge, and so, a healing draught tucked away, they followed young Tessa down to the docks and found their ship, The Horizon, riding at anchor, where I do not doubt this tale of theirs truly begins.
silent_roll: The company agreed under a zone of truth not to disclose the matter within Waterdeep or the surrounding lands.
Anton alone tried to resist the zone of truth and failed.
Azlund gave Vex a sending stone to report the company's progress.

title: The Pickle, the Cheese, and the Storm
summary: Ah, the crossing toward Chult aboard The Horizon, where I confess the finest theatre unfolded not in swordplay but inside a pickle barrel. The company came aboard under the watchful eye of Rindal, and the first evenings passed pleasantly enough, with young Chumble singing for his supper and earning himself a free beer while stout Grieg bested Corwin at sparring for a silver piece. Yet a shadow crept into the galley when Pip the cook found a wheel of cheese gone missing and a bootprint far too large to be Pip's own, a small mystery I dearly hope to see resolved in some later chronicle of mine. Stranger still, Chumble spent a whole night hidden in the brine and woke to find his familiar reborn as a small pickle he christened Wickles, a companion I shall never tire of mentioning. Then the storm that Odele had feared came howling down, and the company answered it magnificently, Vex leaping to snatch Kessra from the waves as Anton braced him, Urida's unseen hand steadying both a loose crate and the wheel, and Grieg holding the ship to her course until the sea relented and a grateful captain draped a cloak of billowing across their shoulders.
silent_roll: No creatures were slain this session.
Urida set an Alarm on the ship's stores overnight.
The company met the storm with six successes and no failures.
The missing wheel of cheese remains unexplained.

title: Suspicions Aboard, Sahuagin at the Rail
summary: Even a chronicler of my standing knows a ship at sea breeds gossip as surely as it breeds rats, and this crossing gave the company plenty to chew upon. Vex drew the passenger Corwin into talk of Port Nyanzaru and its seven merchant princes, learning that Amn had held the city until the princes pried it loose a decade past and that Wakanga O'Tamu might be the finest of the lot, while Urida marked that the man rang false about why he sailed at all. A quiet search of Corwin's cabin turned up nothing a merchant ought to carry and, stranger still, not a scrap of the winter gear any Waterdhavian would keep, and the sailor called Harlen fared no better under Anton's questions, offering names and histories that the hiring manifest plainly gave the lie to. Then the sahuagin came boiling over the rail, and while Corwin and Dragonbait left four of the fish-men dead before the rest could close, Vex and Urida cut down three more between them and sent the raiders back to the deep, the company left a little heavier of purse and a good deal harder for the fight. I will set down here, for later telling, the flashes of blue light behind that crate and how the sea's chill never once seemed to touch Corwin.
silent_roll: Chumble sent Wickle to the fight in his stead rather than going up himself.
The crew suspect Corwin of cheating at dice because he never removes his gloves.
Harlen had lately begun snoring, bore no sailor's tattoos, and looked too slight for the work.

title: A Stolen Cheese and a Hidden Ring
summary: Aboard a ship but two days out from Chult, my little goblin friend Chumble Crudluck set the whole affair spinning with a scheme of rare cunning, an arm wrestling contest contrived for no reason but to pry the ever-gloved Corwin out of his coverings. Fortune smiled crookedly that day, for Chumble threw down Dragonbait and won nothing but a sudden bloom of roses, while Grieg toppled Corwin, who bared his right hand alone and showed nothing worth the trouble. Yet in a later confidence Corwin let slip to Chumble that his hidden left hand cradles an artifact hunted by dangerous men, a secret that soon spilled into the open when the company, chasing a common cheese thief of all things, put the screws to a sailor named Harlen and unmasked him as a Zhentarim agent stowed away in that man's place. They clapped the spy in manacles down in the galley, where he cheerfully owned up to the pilfered cheese as well and warned that his masters were already summoned and would not be far behind. And then came the revelation I have been saving for you, dear reader, for Corwin dropped the whole room to a killing frost and confessed himself to be none other than Artus Cimber, bearer of the fabled Ring of Winter, bound for Chult first to seek his lost wife through Saja N'baza and now, he swears, to stand with this ragged company against the Soulmonger and the Death Curse, even as he braced them for a Zhentarim reckoning within the day.
silent_roll: Chumble tried to kick down Harlen's door and was knocked flat when it rebounded into his face.
Urida and Grieg noticed two bags stowed under Harlen's bunk, one more than any other sailor kept.
Asked why they were each bound for Chult, Chumble said he did not know, Grieg said to help rich people, Anton would not say, and Urida told everything.

Dragonbait smelled of brimstone and then roses at the arm wrestling, of honeysuckle at talk of the Death Curse, of baked bread after elbowing Corwin, and of ham when the company met with Artus Cimber.

title: Cast Clear of a Losing Deck
summary: Volo could tell you of a hundred nights at sea, but few close as this one did. When the pirates came swarming over the rails in the dark, our company met them with a savagery I confess delighted me, Grieg heaving one poor wretch off the deck to shatter on the dinghy below and hacking a grappling rope to slow the tide, Vex severing a second line to pinch the boarders into a killing corridor before setting to work with his scimitar, Urida singing foes to their toll and unmaking others with missiles of force, and little Chumble ending the last with a lash of eldritch fire. Yet numbers are a cruel arithmetic, and when both ends of the ship were drowning in blades and even Grieg had been dropped by dagger work, it was Artus Cimber who made the choice that lingers in me still. He would not spend them all guarding a crew, so he pressed them toward their greater purpose, unfurled a scroll, and cast the company clear, the last sight afforded them being Artus wheeling to loose a mountain of ice from that famous ring upon the massed pirates. They landed hardened and a rung higher for the ordeal in the Harbor Ward of Port Nyanzaru, where a bulletin board offered pirate captains to be hunted and three jungle guides for hire, Eku and Salida and the one who caught their fancy, Musharib. Then the city bared its teeth, for Urida had scarcely secured a diamond for her spellcraft in the Jewel Market when a barrel loosed from a rooftop nearly finished what the pirates could not, a yuan-ti pureblood slinking away from the deed while invisible Wickle trailed it to some shuttered estate, and Chumble's healing so moved a bystander that she spoke of a certain Grandfather Zitembe at the Temple of Savras, a name I suspect these pages have not heard the last of. They closed the day wiser and better armed, Grieg with a new staff in hand and a warm bed apiece at the Thundering Lizard.
silent_roll: Grieg was knocked unconscious by dagger attacks and later healed by Wickle.
Urida was struck by a thrown dagger during the boarding.
Urida was knocked unconscious by the falling barrel and healed by Chumble.

title: The Great Dinosaur Race of Nyanzaru
summary: They set out that morning meaning to call upon the wizard Wakanga and got no further than the first triceratops to blunder into their path. What began with Vex mistaking a beast's horn for a pickpocket's hand ended, as these things so often do, with the whole company hiring reptiles and flinging themselves into the weekly dinosaur races of Port Nyanzaru, all on the word of a tabaxi racer named Lilac Mist and her Fluffy. I will note, with the modesty for which I am justly celebrated, that they had the great fortune to cross my own path near the Temple of Savras, where I sold them a copy of my peerless Guide to Monsters and pressed upon them the hard truths of Chult that no tourist map contains. The race itself was a splendid disaster, for Vex's ornery tyrannosaur Scarback nearly pitched a rival off a bridge before belly-flopping into a water trench and out of contention, while Urida turned aside a jet from Gond's own fountain with a flick of the unseen hand and Grieg hurled a canoe beneath a charging rival's feet. Lilac carried the day and squandered a fifth of her purse on a stolen monkey before the ink was dry, yet it was steady Grieg who limped home third and bore off Ubtao's Ring, a prize made for any who mean to ride the great lizards of this jungle, as I strongly suspect this lot very much intend to do.
silent_roll: Grieg won Ubtao's Ring, which aids survival checks and animal handling involving dinosaurs.
The company bought a copy of Volo's Guide to Monsters.
The party rented three race dinosaurs: Jungle Princess (Urida), Banana Candy (Grieg), and Scarback (Vex).

title: A Journal, a Guide, and Restless Dead
summary: Ah, Port Nyanzaru, where the coin stays snug behind the walls while the dead do the knocking without. My adventurers came back to the Thundering Lizard to find its bulletin board papered with bounties for the likes of Azaka Stormfang and Hew Hackinstone, faces they half knew already, and over cups the innkeeper filled their ears with the sorry state of the Order of the Gauntlet and the strutting Flaming Fist, who from Fort Belurian now demand a body show paperwork or show his heels. The prize of the day was the wizard Wakanga O'tamu, whose villa hums with music no minstrel plays and glows with lights no lamp feeds, and who took such a shine to Urida that he pressed a journal into her hands and set her after some enchanted thing buried in the green. Less charmed was the guide Musharib, who heard their tale of hounding pirates for gold and grudge, sniffed at it, and would not shave a copper from his fee, so off to Hrakhamar through the jungle they agreed to trudge, insect repellent and rain catchers and all. Yet the night's true drama came when alarm bells rang in Malar's Throat and the company waded into a temple of Tymora crawling with skeletons, zombies, and a ghoul, leaving the holy floor swept of the walking dead and their purses a shade heavier for it, all while jungle whispers of a minotaur city gone over to snake folk hinted at chronicles I shall surely tell in time.
silent_roll: Wakanga O'tamu gave Urida a journal and asked her to retrieve a magical object from the jungle in exchange for a reward.
The company agreed to hire Musharib as their guide and to travel overland to Hrakhamar.
Coin was recovered from the temple of Tymora after the fight.

title: Merchant Princes and a Whispered Name
summary: Provisioned at last with fresh barrels and a canoe, our company called upon old Grandfather Zitembe, only to find the poor priest hemmed in by three armed bravos all baying after that elusive Artus Cimber, a name I confess sets even my quill aquiver. Lilac, ever the diplomat with a purse to match, pressed a donation into his hands and coaxed from him both a catalogue of the merchant princes who truly rule Port Nyanzaru and, on a second visit, a vision of a jungle city far to the south, ringed in cliffs and crawling with serpents beneath a black obelisk draped in vines. Between these audiences the streets fairly overflowed with fortune, for the seer Inete engaged them toward the Aldani Basin, the gold-scaled harbormaster Zindar blessed their passage and dangled the promise of pirates for braver days, and the redoubtable Undril Silvertusk struck a bargain to be borne to Camp Vengeance. And the gossip, oh the gossip, of a plateau ghost village emptied of its people, a vanished Halruaan airship called the Star Goddess, and a house-sized turtle king crusted with gems, morsels I shall surely return to devour in later chronicles. Yet the finest stroke came unbidden, when a stranger reeled from the market to collapse against Chumble with a whispered charge to seek the wise guardian of Orolunga east of Mbala, then woke the next morning remembering nothing of the secret he had passed along.
silent_roll: Bought two barrels and a canoe on Musharib's advice.
Accepted Inete's job to escort her to the Aldani Basin to investigate her red-robed wizard visions.
Accepted Undril Silvertusk's request to escort her to Camp Vengeance.
Agreed to buy a second canoe, which Undril will help finance after they arrive.
Zindar asked the party to help deal with pirates when they are ready.
The collapsed fortune-teller was found uninjured and was left to rest at the inn.

title: The Ring in the Rotting Colossus
summary: They lingered a day in town while the sun hammered Chult flat, and there a tabaxi minstrel wheedled a gold piece apiece from Lilac Mist and Chumble Crudluck to fund her gambling, then returned improbably flush to press ten coins on each of them. Once the heat broke they filled their barrel to the brim of what Mr. Stompy could bear and struck out along the beach for the river Soshenstar, past fishing pteranodons and a night sky crossed by quetzalcoatlus, harried all the while by thieving flocks of flying monkeys who made off with pens and oil and a dagger before the company answered with crossbow and mage hand. But the tale I shall carry to my dying day is the dead tyrannosaurus lying split open in a tributary Musharib had blundered them down, its belly a nest of three lurking zombies and one glinting ring, which the party plucked free by the sublime cowardice of Chumble's scheme, a lasso in Wickles' little hands and Grieg and Vex hauling the shiny corpse to the boat to be quietly slain while its fellows slept on. Raxyg's Ring went to Grieg for the light it sheds, and the road unspooled from there through gossiping brontosaurus who murmured of undead, a foolhardy bite of Dancing Monkey Fruit that set Chumble jigging until Undril purged the poison, and one last, smaller mob of monkeys that Lilac Mist simply talked into slinking away. They now sit a single hex from Fort Righteous, that fallen keep of the Order of the Gauntlet, and I promise you the ruin holds a chapter I shall relish telling.
silent_roll: Grieg now carries Raxyg's Ring, which sheds twenty feet of bright light on a spoken command word.
Chumble ate a Dancing Monkey Fruit, was poisoned, and Undril cleared it with lesser restoration.
The party ended the session one hex from Fort Righteous with water topped off by rain catchers.

title: Camp Righteous and the Crocodile's Trials
summary: At crumbling Camp Righteous, that mildewed shrine to the old house of the crocodile whose legend Musharib recounted for the company by the boats, they found only ruin, mold, and a corpse gone soft in the latrine, and I confess I could already smell a better tale waiting behind the temple doors. In they went at Undril Silvertusk's stubborn insistence, and oh, what a gauntlet the place made of poor Vex and Grieg, a pit that swallowed them both, blades they cleverly jammed shut with pitons, and a floor of cursed tiles that blasted the pair senseless again and again until Undril's mercies hauled them back from death's own doorstep. Only when the two battered souls stopped fighting the shrine and crossed in the very manner of man and crocodile did the last door yield, the stair climb, and a humble brown jug fall into their keeping. Staggering back into daylight they were set upon by ten goblins and their boss Yokka, who wanted the spoils and meant to have them over the party's corpses, yet eight of the band fell, and Grieg's killing stroke was cheated when the cunning wretch yanked one of her own into its path. Clinging to three breaths of life, Yokka bought her freedom with word of undead lurking south of the river and a nastier tribe to the north, and the company, grown harder and surer of themselves for the ordeal, sent her off to Port Nyanzaru to peddle her frightful masks, a small mercy I suspect will return to this chronicle before long.
silent_roll: Musharib and Inete stayed with the boats while the rest went inside.
They recovered an amulet of Torm from the shrine.
They took a warhammer and a small purse of gold from the dead man in the latrine.
Lilac Mist released the captured axebeak after her attempt to speak with it failed.
Chumble Crudluck woke from a strange dream.
Urida read the wizard's journal.

title: The Rot at Camp Vengeance
summary: Down the river the company pressed toward Camp Vengeance, hardened by the long road and each grown into deeper arts, pausing only at an abandoned campsite that gave up liquor, traveling gear, and clean water for the taking. What they found at Vengeance was no fortress but a wound in the jungle, all mud and starving goats and soldiers with no fight left in them, their charge Undril Silvertusk delivered at last only to be berated by the grim commander Niles Breakbone and packed off to tend the dying. While the good Lilac Mist worked small miracles of berry and goodwill upon two dozen despairing men, sharper eyes turned to the scout Wulf Rygor, whose tent bred headaches and dizziness and hid a strange growing thing wrapped, so the arcane sight revealed, in a powerful charm that none could name. Sent west to blood some green recruits against the walking dead, the party cut down a knot of Order of the Gauntlet soldiers rotted and threaded through with vine, and as they fought a voice pressed into Urida's mind bidding her use fire, while up in the trees waited a half-mad elven woman who named herself the mother, spoke of a dead shrine whose magic now lived in the plant, and begged in the same breath that they kill it and save it with fire and dark and the divine. Mark that name and that plant, dear reader, for I have a chronicler's certainty we have not heard the last of either, and mark too the columns of smoke and the clamor of battle that met the company as they came home to the palisade.
silent_roll: Grieg advanced and took up the Echo Knight path.
Vex advanced and became a Banneret.
Chumble bound himself to a fiend patron.
Urida advanced and learned shatter.
The company salvaged four sound sets of chainmail and one damaged set from the fallen guards.

title: The Fall of Camp Vengeance
summary: Wickles crept through the ash to find Camp Vengeance a ruin of smoke and corpses, with Ord Firebeard and Undril Silvertusk already trading blows against treacherous guards inside a tent, and our company swept round to the front to put the veteran and his three men down where they stood. From Ord they learned the whole calamity had been sown by Niles Breakbone and Wulf Rygor, who had fled north, and so northward the party pressed until they came upon poor wounded Perne Salhana, who gasped out word of a cave and the husks that lurked within it. Ah, but here is the beat I savor, for it was no simple treachery at all: a yellow musk creeper clinging to the cavern ceiling had Niles in its charm, and when Wickles opened with a flask of oil and the company's fire magic burned the vile plant to nothing, the poor man came back to his wits even as Wulf Rygor and his shambling musk zombies fought on to the bitter last. Walking home, a shaken Niles stammered out the tale of how it had all come to pass, and a grateful Ord set his pen to a letter of commendation for the general at Port Nyanzaru. With the camp emptied to the river and its survivors bound for home, our heroes turned their eyes north once more toward evil goblins and a certain magic journal, though their guide Musharib, ever the practical soul, would want rather more coaxing and coin before he would stray from the safe path.
silent_roll: The party handed over the captured suits of armor and their spare canoe in exchange for Ord Firebeard's written account of their deeds for the general at Port Nyanzaru.
Musharib refused to head north for nothing and required his usual daily rate for travel off the marked path.

title: The Soshenstar's Many Hungers
summary: I have seen rivers turn traitor before, but rarely so gleefully as the Soshenstar, which flung the company from their canoe into a churn of crocodile teeth and left five of them nursing throat leeches for their trouble, a misery only rest and Undril Silvertusk's healing arts could unpick. North they pressed, and here the jungle staged its cruelest theatre, a man staked out and glazed in honey while ants stripped his arm to the bone, whom our heroes snatched from death only to hear him spin a limp tale of goblins before confessing he was a thief caught reaching for an amulet he should have left alone. That he then tottered off toward town on the strength of his own boasting tells you all you need know of explorers, a breed of which I know something. Their guide Musharib, bless his hopeless sense of direction, promptly led them northwest into the coils of a constrictor snake before stumbling back onto the true path. And at the last they cut down a knot of cannibals feasting on a zombie's carrion, each brow painted with a blue triangle that Chumble named for Dendar the Night Serpent, a name I shall want you to remember when this chronicle grows darker.
silent_roll: Vex, Grieg, Chumble Crudluck, Musharib, and Inete contracted throat leeches after the river fight. Urida made the save and Lilac Mist was on shore.
Rest cured Inete and Grieg. Undril Silvertusk used lesser restoration on the others before the Order soldiers continued to Port Nyanzaru.
Musharib was infested during the ant fight and Chumble healed him back to consciousness.
The freed explorer marked the spot of a goblin camp before leaving to find his boat.
Musharib was attacked by a constrictor snake but escaped.

title: The Warren That Flew Away
summary: Even the jungle seemed to boil the day my companions pressed on toward the honeyman's promised site, where a priest of Mielikki named Nuanwa Olerro and three scouts of the Emerald Enclave shared shade and grim news that the walking dead, not the goblins, are the true rot of Chult, and that brave Camp Vengeance has fallen. They came at last upon a ruined clearing hung with skull-chimes and questioned a wounded brontosaurus, who gave up its own wisdom along with the spear pulled from its flank and swore the goblins had simply flown away, a riddle half-answered by a great cut vine and a tall tree bruised along its northeastern side. I must record, with a chronicler's fond exasperation, that their attempt to boil poison from dancing monkey fruit yielded nothing but a camp full of choking fumes and the humbling lesson that such alchemy wants an alembic. Come the cool of the next morning they crept upon the goblin warren of Yellyark beneath a silencing charm their guide Musharib had woven, and might have kept their surprise had Vex not tired of the waiting and loosed the first arrow himself, waking the whole nest to war. They cut down a score of goblins and put Lilac Mist's arrow through Queen Grabstab, yet the cunning wretches slashed a hidden vine and flung all Yellyark skyward toward the southeast, carrying the dead queen and the amulet at her throat clean out of reach, a theft I promise you shall echo in chronicles yet to come.
silent_roll: Vex breathed fire into a hut sheltering goblin children, and Urida's shatter killed those who survived.
At least six goblin children died there.

title: Ashes of Yellyark, a Guardian Half-Woken
summary: I confess a chronicler seldom relishes a graveyard, yet even I would have paused at what remained of Yellyark, beaten into utter wreckage with not one soul left breathing, where the company sifted the ruin, drew Queen Grabstab's command amulet from her cold remains, and gathered the fallen into some rough semblance of a funeral. The road that followed gave one quiet day and then a wicked night, for in the small hours five eblis swept down upon the camp and snatched Inete into the air, until Wickles' watchfulness roused Chumble Crudluck and the whole company besides, who felled the thief mid-flight and left their friend bruised from the drop but breathing. Three of the bird-fiends died before the surviving pair thought better of the business and bought their lives with a whispered map, which led to a ring tucked in a hollow tree, a trifling prize but honestly won. A creeping blue mist tried the party next, some forty feet of it drifting across their path, though Lilac Mist marked it in good time and the company slipped around rather than through. And at the last they found Vorn, that guardian of no small mystery, who stirred only when Urida drew near and even then answered but half its purpose, a great sentinel that walks and follows yet cannot strike nor ward, its power dwindled to embers beside a nameless skeleton and a mud-caked box of strange beast-faced carvings whose old magic had all but guttered out.
silent_roll: Queen Grabstab's command amulet was recovered from the wreckage of Yellyark.
Inete was snatched aloft by an eblis and fell about twenty feet but survived.
Two eblis were spared in exchange for the location of a hidden ring worth roughly fifty gold.
Vorn responds only when Urida is near and is only partially operational. It can walk and follow but cannot attack, store spells, or protect, and it heals only ten points a day.
A weak, nearly spent transmutation lingers on the mud-caked box, and it can be slotted into the guardian, though doing so produced no visible change.
The company plans to return to Port Nyanzaru to resupply.

title: Long Road Home and the Dinosaur Races
summary: The company's long march out of the deep jungle opened with a lesson in caution, for when Grieg caught the reek of carrion at a narrow canyon and poor Wickles was plucked from the sky by a hungry vine, the wise travellers simply walked the long way round. A gentler meeting followed in an almiraj, that shy one-horned hare, which Lilac soothed with honeyed animal-speech until it hopped trustingly into Vex's pack, and there I daresay it rides still. The river bore them back toward Port Nyanzaru, and though a giant boa constrictor chanced its luck against Vex mid-voyage, it slid away wounded into the dark water after Chumble's crackling blast, leaving the company to a well-earned spell of commerce, a scimitar sent off for enchanting and an alchemist's kit tucked away. Yet it is the dinosaur races that shall crown this chapter, where amid a farting triceratops, a plodding stegosaurus, and a banana dangled on a pole, our own Lilac Mist mounted Mr. Stompy to hushed whispers of her return and thundered to her third championship and a heavy purse of gold. And on that triumphant evening, as steadfast Musharib laid down his post to linger in town, a sly fellow named Rokah slipped from the shadows with a proposition wrapped in stolen charters and roguish promises, a hook I shall gladly leave dangling for my next telling.
silent_roll: No creatures were slain on this leg of the journey.
Wickles was snatched from the air by a vine, and the group detoured around the canyon rather than fight through the vines.
A giant boa constrictor seized Vex aboard the boat but could not pull him from it. Chumble wounded it with eldritch blast before it dove underwater and escaped.
The almiraj was calmed and befriended rather than killed and now rides in Vex's backpack.
The shield guardian was left a short way into the jungle, covered in roots and moss.

title: The Long Road to Shilku Bay
summary: Before the company quit the trading post they kitted themselves out in earnest, a keener scimitar, a stouter shield, arrows that bite truer, and the ever-blessed insect repellent, while young Grieg let go his old shield and the whole table traded a whispered rumor of a ruined city up the River Tath, guarded past Kahakla Gorge by a naga said to be both wise and generous. They signed on to escort a fellow named Rokah to Fort Beluarian, he footing their passage aboard the Pegasus, and once there they circled the walls like foxes about a henhouse and found no way to slip inside without inviting their own slaughter. Liara Portyr of the Flaming Fist put them to better use with bounties on ghoul heads, a mystery of monstrous footprints in the southern jungle, and the darkened silence of Shilku, and it was Shilku they chose to answer first. The sharpest ears among them caught wind of a man who reeked of ham and unraveled him to be Dragonbait himself, a dragon-man whose wrecked crew had begged passage home while one lonely prisoner went strangely unaccounted for. Then, with the guide Shago engaged and a Baldurian deck beneath them, they bought their way past the greedy Aremag with a scrape of coin and Vex's honeyed Draconic, Chumble tossing the tribute clean into the beast's maw, and by the time the coast fell away behind them the long road had hardened this company into something more dangerous than when first I met them.
silent_roll: Chumble Crudluck had a dream on the first night out.
Qawasha declined to guide the party for now, offering to join once they turn to fighting the undead.
Rokah took the failure at the fort badly and went back into the jungle with his companions rather than to his ship.
Wickles trailed Rokah's group afterward and marked that they were not heading back to their vessel.

title: A Kindness Too Large by Half
summary: Begin with the captain's apology, for it is the crooked thread running through this whole affair. The company overheard him quarrelling with his first mate over the tribute paid to Aremag. He offered back double what they had fed that dragon turtle, to be handed over when he collects them again. Then he put them ashore south of Shilku, clear of the volcanic debris raining down that coast, and left them a sending stone. Three days' notice, he said, and he would come. Generous. Suspiciously so. They walked north and found Shilku quiet above and stubbornly alive beneath, where Sithi Vinecutter opened a hatch and a history together. Her people want Hrakhamar back from the firenewts, and the treasury will answer for it. She asked after two scouts as well, Laz Drumthunder and Malkar Stonegrist, overdue out of the Valley of Lost Honor. On the road out, a salamander came at the company, and Chumble Crudluck unmade it with eldritch fire. Thirty miles short of Hrakhamar, Grieg finally set the pieces side by side. Days of sailing, a wait of any length, a voyage home, all freely given, and never one word about pirates. I have known cheaper kindnesses to cost a great deal more.
silent_roll: Vex found a knife cut from a tyrannosaurus tooth, and the hatch that led down into the Shilku Outpost.
Helga Ironfist mended Chumble Crudluck and Grieg after the two sparred over a new stick of Chumble's.
Helga also passed on word of a book to the left of the two iron men, holding the secrets needed to acquire the gauntlet.
Grieg drew honey from the alchemy jug for the bartender Yutmus Treasurehead, who spoke of an airship seen crashing north of Shilku.
Barendd Torunn was dug out of a collapsed passage, given Mardred Ungart's adamantine pick, and paid the company in gems.
Rurik Vinecutter asked them to gather Ohelo berries on their travels.
Obsidian shards taken from the salamander, a ruby candelabra, and an ivory staff carved as a snake went into the common fund.
The company rested a night in the outpost's guest quarters before setting out.
Falling volcanic debris had to be dodged twice on the road toward Hrakhamar.

title: What They Carried Out of Hrakhamar
summary: They went to Hrakhamar to break the firenewts. They came out carrying two dwarves instead, and I call that the better bargain. The forge is a furnace with walkways strung above it, and I would not cross those gantries for any fee you could name. Grieg solved the problem the way an echo knight solves everything, by sending himself ahead in pieces and rigging ropes for the rest. What they found inside has kept me awake since. A cube of iron that opens like a book, and set inside it two indentations shaped for keys. They also found a chunk of adamantine key, smashed into a crude statue, which they pocketed without ceremony. Then the firenewts came at them. Lilac Mist put an arrow through one, and Urida's shatter took another apart. Vex met a smoke mephit with his scimitar, and Chumble sent Wickles after the second. Behind all of it sat Laz and Malkar, the scouts Sithi Vinecutter had asked them to find, alive and hollowed to the bone. The company could have pressed deeper and taken the forge entire. They chose instead to walk their ruined dwarves back out into the ash and let them rest. Mark that restraint. It is newer than they are.
silent_roll: Urida found ohelo berries on the road to the forge, the fruit Rurik Vinecutter had asked for.
Chumble Crudluck ate one on the spot to test it for poison. It was not poison.
A red dragon was seen flying in the skies to the southwest during the march.
Obsidian taken from the firenewts and the mephits went into the party's shared funds.

title: Taking Hrakhamar Back by Thirds
summary: The company went back into Hrakhamar to drive the firenewts out of it, which was the work Sithi Vinecutter had hired them for. Understand that they had first spent two nights at the door and the day between them, waiting, and the mountain used those hours better than they did. The firenewts had counted their dead by then. Sentries on giant striders now watched the main entrance and the passage from Wyrmheart Mine. Worse, a ritual was already gathering on Mount Todra. So the reckoning came dearer than it needed to be. Lilac Mist answered with three arrows and a scimitar, three newts and a strider fallen to her alone. Grieg drove his trident through a strider, then through a warlock of Imix. Shago earned every coin of his wage twice over, four warriors and two striders dead by his hand. Fire came at them in gouts, spat by newt and mount alike. They danced through it. The guard set around the statue of Imix broke next. Behind them Sithi Vinecutter's dwarves held the door and kept two broken scouts breathing. A third of the forge was theirs when they finally sat down to rest. Wickles, invisible, had already walked the whole of what remained, and the taking of Hrakhamar was only begun.
silent_roll: Laz confirmed the runes in the dwarven molds read beginning and ending.
Sithi Vinecutter came up from the Shilku Outpost with six companions, a smith and a priest among them.
Helga Ironfist used lesser restoration on Malkar to quiet him.
Obsidian worth 131 gp went into the slush fund.

title: A Hundred Years, Handed Back
summary:
Every dwarf in Chult knows how the story of Hrakhamar goes. A company marches on the forge, and the forge kills them, and it has gone that way for a hundred years. This time the dwarves stayed at the door, because this time they had strangers to send in, and the strangers did not know the story was supposed to end badly. The firenewts nearly taught them. Chumble Crudluck went down in the first press of fire. If Lilac Mist had been a heartbeat slower, the company would have carried a body out of the mountain instead of a victory. She was not slower. Twice she was not. And because the goblin kept getting up, the rod he carries kept feeding, one rune waking for every enemy his blasts unmade. Four lights burn on it now, where one burned before. That was the arithmetic that broke the firenewts: a company that would not stay down, and a hired guide, Shago, who out-killed every blade in it.

So when Sithi Vinecutter walked into halls her people lost a century ago, she owed the crossing to outlanders, and she paid as dwarves pay. Everything. Mardred's fire-resistant craft. The treasury's iron. And the one thing no dwarf could give away outright, Moradin's Gauntlet, she lent, theirs to carry while they walk Chult and sworn to come home to the dwarves after. Her condition was blunt as its giver: do not die and leave it in some hole. The price of the rest was the war, that the strangers finish the story, north through Mount Todra, all the way to the red dragon in Wyrmheart Mine. They agreed, knowing what no dwarf yet knows, that the story runs longer than Hrakhamar. The firenewts had a patron. Lilac Mist heard them speak his name. Withers.
silent_roll: The company emptied the armory into a side tunnel before the dwarves came down with their thanks.
Grieg claimed a set of half plate from the haul and was wearing it by the time the thanking started.
The treasury opened only after Mardred reforged its ruined keys. Inside sat iron and adamantine ingots by the thousand.

title: The Gnome Who Calmed the Mountain
summary:
Understand what the firenewts had been building toward all this time. Not the forge. The forge was only ever the doorstep. The morning after the company won it back, Mount Todra put on a black and churning crown, raining volcanic fire while earthquakes rattled Hrakhamar's halls, and Sithi Vinecutter asked them to climb with her and end it. The mountain fought them the whole way up. A landslide buried Lilac Mist and Urida, and Grieg and Chumble Crudluck dug them out with their hands. A magma jet caught Chumble and Vex. Sulfuric gas dropped Chumble where he stood, and Urida fed him the ohelo berry that brought him back. Mark the little wizard. She spent the climb being buried and reviving the fallen, and the summit had not yet begun to ask its price.

At the caldera three warlocks of Imix stood chanting above the crater, and the company attacked too late by a breath. The ritual closed and the Aspect of Imix rose out of the fire, a phoenix of pure flame wearing a god's anger. Bolts from Grieg and Vex unmade two of the warlocks and Shago's bow answered for the rest. The Aspect struck Urida down. Grieg got Lilac Mist's healing potion into her, and she stood back up, and then the rock gnome put a volley of magic missiles through a fragment of the Elemental Prince of Fire. The whole mountain exhaled. The lava sank home. The strangest wounds came at the mountain's foot, after. Shago cheerfully let slip that the Flaming Fist will expect half of everything the company has gained. Half. And Sithi pressed them toward Tzindelor, the red dragon of Wyrmheart Mine, a war they promised her in the warmth of victory and now, sober, call a suicide mission. Ten days of jungle lie between them and the tej at Shilku Outpost. I suspect it will taste of arithmetic.
silent_roll: Mardred prepared fire-resistant plates and patches for the company's armor, to be collected on the way back through Hrakhamar.
Grieg paid 50 gp from the slush fund to have the muffled trait added to his half plate.
105 gp of obsidian recovered at the caldera went to the slush fund.
The return trip to Shilku Outpost takes ten days, and the next session starts there.
The party plans to recall the Flaming Fist ship and return to Fort Beluarian, paying the Fist's half for now.

title: Mostly Honest at Fort Beluarian
summary:
Understand what the company did at Fort Beluarian, because it took more nerve than the volcano. Liara Portyr had a month's worth of questions and a soldier's arithmetic, and when she asked for a tally of what Chult had yielded, they gave her one. A mostly honest one. Everything went on her table, adamantine ingots, captured steel, a heap of gold, everything but the half plate already buckled on Grieg's back and Moradin's Gauntlet, which no ledger in that fort ever heard named. The Fist took its cut, near forty parts in a hundred, and handed the steel straight to its soldiers. In return came a charter of exploration, permanent rooms, potions and scrolls, and a warm request to keep hunting ghouls and stranger things to the south. Shago watched the whole performance and said not one word to his paymasters. Afterward he told the company he was astonished they dared and impressed they got away with it, then signed on for another thirty days at a price they could not talk down. He is not Fist, as it turns out. He simply fights where the undead are.

Fire has largely stopped biting them. Mardred's plates and patches turned the whole company fire-resistant before they left the outpost, Vex most of all, and the magmins that tried them on the road to the coast learned it briefly. But mark what they found on the overland walk toward Port Nyanzaru: a rune cut into tree after tree that Vex's magic read as ice, a great pile of dung, and footprints too large for anything that ought to leave them. Frost giants, the company mused, in Chult of all places. Grieg said the quieter thing. The Ring of Winter. I know that ring's story. Every chronicler does. I do not believe this thread is finished with them.
silent_roll: Wickles twice tried to slip into the Fist's vaults behind Gruta and never got through the door.
The Flaming Fist crew repaid 121 gp for the tribute forced at Aremag's crossing and handled the dragon turtle themselves on the return leg.

The party got the jump on two girallons on the road to Port Nyanzaru and killed them quickly, Lilac Mist's longbow taking one and Shago's spear the other. Their cache held a two-person tent, two healing kits, and a vial of wyvern poison.
Another ohela bush yielded 16 berries, and five magmins left 70 gp of obsidian for the slush fund.
Liara Portyr repositioned tokens on her map of Chult. The Fist intends to move on Hrakhamar and Shilku.
The party plans to sell off goods in Port Nyanzaru, show Musharib the Gauntlet, then continue down the River Soshenstar.

title: A Writ, a Gauntlet, and Three Roads
summary:
The company came back to Port Nyanzaru on the twenty-seventh of Eleint, overland from Fort Beluarian, with a coast's worth of plunder to sell and Moradin's Gauntlet, the dwarves' loan, on Vex's hand. Musharib, their first guide in Chult, was at the inn with a new company that had just taken him on. He had not been impressed by their experience when they first hired him months before, but as Vex extended his hand in greeting, the gauntlet glinting on it, and told him how they had taken Hrakhamar back for the dwarves, he had no choice but to be impressed.

Nobody in the Great Souk would buy wyvern poison, so they carried the vial to Jessamine, and while her daughter Ymezra tested it they told her what they had come to Chult to do, investigate the death curse and end it. That impressed her more than it should have, and the company understood why without her saying it: the curse is in her too. Once the poison was confirmed she raised her offer, the extra for the cause, and it was into that warmth that Chumble Crudluck asked whether anyone needed killing. She had to be talked into it, but she let them see the writs she held open. One named an Omala at the Dye Works. The other named Shago.

They declined both and went back to the inn to find their guide. Shago had gone his own way in the city on business he called personal, and he had let it be known that he had no love for Jessamine, and when they told him he was marked for death he was not surprised. He showed them an iron token that he said meant exactly that, and that he took for a mistake, though he could not say who would want him dead. The company did not ask him where he had been. I would have.

They left the next day, down the Soshenstar, and two weeks later stood on the plateau at Mbala, where buildings once stood and now one hut does. A ziggurat of four tiers rose to the west and a ball of earth hung in the sky to the east. To the south Lilac Mist picked out the wreck of an airship, seen through a mask she had bought in the city from Yokka, the goblin they had spared at Camp Righteous and sent there to sell masks. Months ago in that same city a man fell against Chumble in the market and whispered to him to seek the wise guardian of Orolunga, east of Mbala. The company means to search the hut first, and then the ziggurat. I have been at this long enough to know when a chronicle is about to turn.
silent_roll: Musharib's new company is the one the party saw returning to Port Nyanzaru a couple of months back: a shield dwarf, a goliath ranger, a human cleric, and a tiefling wizard. They had meant to sail for Hrakhamar and will go to Kitcher's Inlet instead, to explore the River Olung and perhaps Kir Sabal for clues to the Soulmonger.
Jessamine's offer for the wyvern poison rose from 500 to 700 gp once Ymezra confirmed it.
The west coast haul was sold in the Great Souk. Chumble Crudluck traded his leather armor for studded leather.
Purchases: a +1 trident from Ekene-Afa, a +1 grimoire for Urida from Wakanga O'tamu, healing potions for everyone, and insect repellent topped up to ten apiece. Ekene-Afa was asked to find a +1 bow.
The company convinced Wakanga O'tamu that Urida had made no progress on finding the control amulet.

Yokka runs her mask shop with Eemux and Rork. Lilac Mist's mask carries the Eyes of the Eagle enchantment, and Yokka said most of the price went to Wakanga O'tamu for the magic. She was gleeful to hear the goblins of Yellyark had been destroyed.
Inete has lost her appetite for adventure.
An eighty-foot bank of blue mist was sighted on 26 Eleint and avoided. Grung were seen fleeing from the party on the Soshenstar.

title: The Last Survivor of Mbala
summary:
There are two ways to be the last soul left in a dead village. One is luck. Mark the other. Nanny Pu'pu, in the hut at Mbala's southern edge, said the pterafolk had killed everyone but her, and spared her only for being too stringy. She offers to raise the dead, and hers, she says, still get up, whatever trouble others are having. Understand what that boast was to a company sent across the sea because the dead have grown harder and harder to call back. That is the Death Curse. Her price for what she knew of Orolunga was the pterafolk dead. While she bargained, Wickles, Chumble Crudluck's familiar, found the clothes piled in her hut cut for several bodies, none hers.

Shago, the company's hired guide, went down the nest's chimney with Lilac Mist and Urida to ambush eight pterafolk while the rest waited above for whatever flew out. It nearly cost two of them. Lilac Mist fell and came back on an Ohelo berry, Urida on a potion Vex dropped on her. The pterafolk talked as they fought: they and the old woman had a standing quarrel over first bite of Mbala's people. The last survivor of Mbala was one of the two things that ate it.

When they rested, Chumble Crudluck found all ten runes lit on the mysterious rod he carries, a new row begun beneath. Vex read them. Soul.

Chumble Crudluck went back to report the pterafolk dead and ask after Orolunga. An evil place, she said, kept by an evil woman they could surely kill, and one of her scales would do as proof. Then her hand went for a hair on the goblin's head, and he caught it. Grieg and Lilac Mist, both covered in hair, both nearest her the first time, did their own arithmetic. The company agreed to look into Orolunga, to appease her, and withdrew.

Five days' travel later, half a mile short of Orolunga's ziggurat, Lilac Mist spotted a camp, its fire still smoking. Empty. As they searched, a voice somewhere said "Oh!", and Vex caught the smell of tar behind him. Dragonbait, who sailed with them from Waterdeep, speaks in scents, and tar is one of his words. And Dragonbait is seldom far from Artus Cimber, who spent a scroll to throw the company clear of a boarded ship and turned to meet the pirates with the Ring of Winter. They have not seen him since, and had every reason to expect him near. That much was expectation. The smell was not. They had not yet turned around, and already knew whose scent that was.
silent_roll: The company reached fifth level after the pterafolk nest.
Two dead explorers in the nest yielded a potion of greater healing and a silver dagger.
Shago killed three pterafolk with his spear, outside the company's own tally.
Urida's detect magic found nothing on Nanny Pu'pu or the things in her hut.
Lilac Mist drew the statue in Mbala.

title: Once in a Lifetime at Orolunga
summary:
Half a mile short of the ziggurat, Lilac Mist had found a small camp, its fire still smoking and no one at it, and then a voice at their backs. The camp was Artus Cimber's and Dragonbait's, the two the company had last seen on the Horizon's deck, turning to face the pirates as Artus's scroll carried everyone else clear. Understand what he is to them. He had told them before that night why he sailed: to ask Saja N'baza, the naga who guards Orolunga, after his lost wife. He and Dragonbait had spoken with her and camped here a week or so since. He could not go with them, because one sees her once in a lifetime and he had spent his. Asked about Nanny Pu'pu of Mbala, who calls the mistress of Orolunga an evil bitch woman and wants one of her scales as proof of a killing, he guessed at what Nanny herself might be: a hag, probably a green one.

Orolunga is a ziggurat of four tiers, and it is not climbed by climbing. The first stair turned dangerous and the company stopped, until Chumble Crudluck announced that a little guy, his words, had shown him the way, and the way was flowers. On the second tier another creature, again seen by the goblin, pointed him to a feather, and on the third a last one showed what both were for. The lesson had a snake in it. With great trepidation they tapped it with the flowers, stroked it with the feather, then lay down and let it slither into their mouths.

In Port Nyanzaru a stranger once fell against Chumble and whispered that the wise guardian of Orolunga could direct them to what they seek. She did. The Soulmonger, the thing that brought this company across the sea, is in Omu, a city hidden under the canopy where Acererak killed and buried nine trickster gods. The death curse that has made the dead so hard to raise ends when Ras Nsi dies: raised so often the curse has him too, Acererak's tool and intended victim, bent on opening a door under the Peaks of Flame to let Dendar the Night Serpent swallow the sun. That much was new. The rest she spent on what they already carried. She read them the legend of the nine gods, and Grieg matched it to the animals on the cube they carry for Vorn, their shield guardian, who may draw his power, she thought, from Omu itself. Shago, the guide hired at Fort Beluarian, carries an iron token, a death mark he called a mistake when a writ on his life surfaced in Port Nyanzaru, and could not say whose. She could. Kwayothe, one of the seven merchant princes, to punish Zhanthi, another. And the rod that turned up unexplained in the goblin's pack, ten runes lit by his kills and a new row Vex read as soul: a Rod of the Pact Keeper, she judged, corrupted by someone she could not name and would not have them trust. Then she reminded him that a warlock's gifts outlive his patron. Mark that she thought he needed to hear it.

Artus met them back at camp with the news that they had been gone all night. Now the company means to go back to Mbala for the hag. Nanny Pu'pu asked for a scale, and reached for a hair from the goblin's head while she asked. I do not think she will be getting either.
silent_roll: Saja N'baza offered each of them a charm. Lilac Mist chose the Charm of Animal Conjuring, and Vex and Grieg each chose the Charm of Restoration. Urida and Chumble Crudluck could not decide and will receive theirs later.
Saja N'baza said the Soulmonger is not yet at full power, but it is close, perhaps a couple of weeks away.

Saja N'baza named the dragon in Wyrmheart Mine, the lich of the Red Wizards of Thay in the Heart of Ubtao, and Dendar the Night Serpent as other powerful opponents. The lich shares their purpose against Ras Nsi and is also looking for Artus Cimber.
Saja N'baza said there are guides in Port Nyanzaru who might help, though not much, and that some the company has already met might help too.
Saja N'baza said Omu lies between the Valley of Lost Honor and the Peaks of Flame and is best seen from the air, and that the aarakocra of Kir Sabal might be able to help since they can fly.

title: The Last Victim at Mbala
summary:
Remember what this company is for. They crossed a sea because the dead had stopped coming back and Azlund asked them to see to it.

They came back up the switchbacks of Mbala and found a man in the dirt before the hut, dragging himself toward them and begging for help, with Nanny Pu'pu standing over him. She looked up, turned, and walked inside as if nothing were wrong.

Grieg went to the man. Urida's shatter blew the hut apart in hides and thatch and reptile ribs, with no body in the wreck and no invisible crone to be found. What found them came from underneath. As Grieg dragged the man clear, a hand broke the earth and closed on his leg, and a flesh golem heaved up behind it. The hag's voice said "drop it now," and a flying monkey let fall a bottle that burst into insects and a lash of lightning that went into the golem and fed it.

They hacked at it, the crone jeering unseen, until Chumble Crudluck's eldritch blast finished it. Then she showed herself on a wall, ready to run, and Lilac Mist put an arrow through her, saw the flinch come a shade late, and guessed it for an illusion. Grieg had one thing left. He had stood in that hut with the woman two weeks before. He shut his eyes and drew the air in, and the scent came, and did not lead him far. It led to the man at his feet. Nanny Pu'pu shed the dying man like a cloak and went for Grieg with her claws. She had staged it from the switchbacks. She had not reckoned on a wulven's nose. She tried to vanish again. Urida guessed where and dropped a fireball on the guess. The hag came back into sight, and Shago's spear ended the last survivor of Mbala.

The fight settled and Mbala cleared, they headed for Port Nyanzaru, only to run into trouble anew. Frost giants on the road reminded Artus Cimber what he wears on his hand, and he stays in Port Nyanzaru with Dragonbait. He points them at Tamalka Village, where someone named Wainrath knows something of the Heart of the Wild, which Saja N'baza told him is corrupted and eating at Chult's magic. And they hired Salida, the guide the naga named as Ras Nsi's, to walk her out past the walls and ask.

That evening Azlund's sending stone spoke in Vex's hand. The Death Curse is in full effect, his cousin said. Skamos and Vander, the storytellers of the House of Healing, have a few months. The hag had them running to a wounded man who was not one. Here are two who are, a sea away, and no one can say how few is few.
silent_roll: 19 Marpenoth, at camp: Artus Cimber said he knows Ras Nsi and has fought him, and had thought him dead. Ras Nsi was a bara of Mezro, is responsible for Chult's undead, and is marked by the purple triangle symbols on some of them.
Artus is from Cormyr, has been to Mezro, and met his wife Alisanda there. She is in Mezro now. Mezro still exists but is not where the map claims.

Saja N'baza told Artus that Mezro returns only when it is safe: Ras Nsi eliminated, and the corrupted Heart of the Wild, now corroding Chult's magic, set right. Artus hopes the Heart is the first step and repeated his Horizon pledge to help against the Death Curse and Ras Nsi.
Artus and Dragonbait came to Mbala with the company at Dragonbait's urging. Travel 20 to 24 Marpenoth, the fight on 25 Marpenoth, travel to Port Nyanzaru 25 Marpenoth to 6 Uktar.
While the hag was hidden, Vex tried his blindsight and Urida her detect magic. Neither found her.
Shago killed Nanny Pu'pu with his spear after Urida's fireball broke her invisibility. NPC kill, not in the ledger.
The patrol avoided late on the road to Port Nyanzaru was three frost giants and two winter wolves.
7 Uktar shopping: +1 longbow to Lilac Mist (500 gp), her old bow to Grieg and a new one to Vex (50 gp), +1 arrows shared among the bow users, two heavy crossbows sold (50 gp).
Salida was hired for 150 gp, Chumble Crudluck and Lilac Mist doing the talking, so she can be questioned outside town and likely killed.

Artus met them at Tiriki Anchorage on 7 Uktar with the location of Tamalka Village and the name Wainrath. He and Dragonbait stay in Port Nyanzaru to avoid the frost giant patrols and continue researching the Heart of the Wild.

title: Smoke Over Tamalka, Strangers Beneath It
summary:
They came to Tamalka for Wainrath's word on the Heart of the Wild, and they saw the smoke before they saw the village. The trees thinned to a path and a clearing, and from a few hundred feet off there were wisps of black smoke over the roofs, a putrid stench in the wet air, and battered dead along the path to the gate. The low wooden wall was burned or broken along most of its length, and within, the huts had been raided and torched, a few villagers lying at their doors, the stench worse among them. The raiders were still among the houses, and fell back into one of them as the company came up.

They survived the spiked pits beyond the archway and came on to the house, where Urida's shatter rang through the walls and took apart one of the raiders inside, and arrows came at them from two bowmen. Chumble Crudluck's eldritch blast answered one and Shago's longbow the other. The stench they had walked through since the path was strongest at a hut whose walls had mostly been knocked flat, and inside was a catoblepas, a bloated beast whose serpentine neck could barely lift its head. It stank of death and swamp gas and skunk musk. Behind the beast stood its keeper, a druid in the reddish and brown the raiders wore. Grieg went in with the trident, and the beast went down under it. Then the trident came again and found the keeper.

That was the last of the raiders, and Wainrath was still not found. In one small house the furniture had been thrown about and the bed tipped on its side, and in the floor where it had stood was an open trapdoor. The passages under it were a maze, and at the end of them was a wide chamber where three people had a fourth under question. One of the three spoke for all of them. "Stay your swords. Surely we could interrogate him together?" The company had come to Tamalka to ask Wainrath a question. Under Tamalka a stranger asked them one instead, and this page ends before they answered it.
silent_roll: Salida left the camp one night on the road to Tamalka, and Wickles followed and saw her do something he could not make out.
A signet ring marked with a scaled claw came off the raiders, and neither Salida nor Shago knew the mark.

title: The Last Warrior of Mezro
summary:
There is a temple in the mountains south of Port Nyanzaru that was built to keep the magic that keeps Chult, and it appeared not to have been kept in years. That much the company had from Wainrath, once Gavori had died on Grieg's trident and the man could talk. The power behind the Heart of the Wild has gone bad, and the jungle with it. The mage hunters who guarded it, the Obanashi, have not been seen in a long time. He gave them a stone that would know the way. Four days out of the port it began to pull, and it drew Chumble Crudluck up a bare mountainside under a noon sun, the mist lying low on the trees below and not a bird or a beast making a sound, to a rune cut in the rock. The rune flared orange and was gone, and where it had been was a doorway into the dark. The one guarding it was no mage hunter. She was a dryad, Nava, who came out of the scrub beside the door so glad of visitors she could hardly keep still, and announced that none passed her without proving their worth, with the door already open at her back. They let her have her tests, and passed them, and were pronounced worthy.

Inside, the temple did what its keeper only played at. Off the entry were four small chambers, in each a statue over an altar, and in each altar a trial with a stone for whoever met it. Grieg went first to the water. The statue was a woman rising out of a column of water, the plaque beneath her a figure bent over a pool, and the altar had been hollowed and filled to the brim with water so clear it had no bottom. He leaned over it and looked down into the abyss, and the abyss looked back, and terror went up his spine and took him. For five minutes he stood in the empty hall talking to no one in words that were not words, while the company waited. After coming back to his senses, he walked to the next chamber, where a reddish figure with hair of carved flame stood over an altar draped in a tapestry of fire, a sun cut into the stone beneath it and a hand burned into the sun's heart, and he put his hand in the print. The heat went up his arm like something alive, and he held, and the statue's base slid open on a smooth piece of red granite. In the third, under a figure with legs of smoke, six fist-sized stones rose at his approach and spun, each throwing lightning into a seventh at the center in a pattern with gaps in it. He watched for the gap, put his hand through it, and came away with the stone. Then Lilac Mist went to the water. She leaned over the basin and looked into whatever waited for her there, for as long as it wanted her to look, and did not look away. The statue's base opened on a piece of lapis lazuli, and it was hers. The last stone was under a squat figure on a crag, and it asked only for patience: a plaque of filled and empty squares, and stone buttons that rose and fell under her hands until they matched it.

Four stones went into four sockets in the iron doors at the back of the shrine, and the doors opened on a hall of scorched walls and fallen stone, and in it, in a temple that seemed abandoned to the wilds, stood one woman, alone. They asked her who she was. "I think I'm the last warrior of Mezro." Mezro, that Artus Cimber told them is not destroyed and not where the map puts it, and will not come back until Chult is safe. Mezro, where Ras Nsi was a bara before he turned. The keepers of Chult's magic have yet to be found, and at the end of their temple stands the last soldier of a city that is not supposed to be anywhere. Or so she thinks. Mark the word.
silent_roll: They found a sending stone on Salida and drowned her in the Soshenstar.
Artus Cimber went after the Obanashi mage hunters himself and sent the company to their temple.
Nava told the company to remember the number 3145.
Nava said no one else had come to the door recently.

title: A Century Late to the Heart
summary:
The woman in the hall called herself Nerissa, and ten days ago, by her count, she was on patrol outside Mezro when a light of every color burned over her, and she woke in the same city, flooded and in ruins. Visions of places have come to her since, and one of them led her here, to stand in front of the company. She takes the visions for Ubtao's, though the company had heard that Ubtao left Chult long ago, and she asked to join them.

Wainrath's stone opened the hall's doors, and down the western way stood a ghostly form they came to find out was Rhoga. She had led the Obanashi, who kept this temple and its Heart. The Heart was a stone, held past the font. A century ago the wizard Kolate tricked her into showing him where it lay, and he drew its power into a coin. She died trying to take it back, and Ubtao, she is sure, holds her here while Kolate still draws breath. A naga held the main hall now, and they went east to kill it.

They came into the Hall of the Rising Sun, the font at its far end, glowing water under an iron sun, and between them and it Hajoka, a spirit naga, cobra-bodied, and his giant constrictor. He sent the snake in among them and worked from behind it, a black ray first, which put Vex on the floor until Grieg got a potion down him, then lightning the length of the hall through most of the company, which dropped Urida until Lilac Mist's potion brought her up. Vex, back on his feet, cut the constrictor apart with his scimitar, and with nothing left in front of him the naga met Chumble Crudluck's eldritch blast, lighting a third rune on his Rod of the Pact Keeper.

Then at the font Wainrath's stone opened a portal in the water, into a space that lay outside the temple altogether. Beyond was green growth ringed by golden mist that lit itself, and by the pool they came out of, an old withered tree. They took it for what was left of the Heart, and rested there in peace, with nothing left to keep.

In time they came back through the portal and out of the temple the way they had come in, and at the cave mouth they heard Artus Cimber before they saw him, in a shouting match with a woman, Xhosala. She argued that he wanted the Heart for his road to Mezro and not for all Chult. They talked her into one effort, no one in it for themselves, and she finished Rhoga's story: the Heart's power, loosed by Kolate in the fight that killed them both, grew into a darkwood tree above the canopy, the Forsaken Tree. She will take them there, a dead tree behind them and the Forsaken Tree ahead.
silent_roll: The blade trap among the columns of the eastern hall, disarmed with Nava's numbers.
A water elemental in the pool at the end of the cave stream drove Grieg back.

title: The Woman Who Was Not Nerissa
summary:
Gentle reader, I have walked into a great many places I was told not to walk into, and I have written about most of them, and I tell you plainly that the hardest thing an adventurer ever does is to turn around. Any fool with a sword can go forward. Going forward is what the sword is for. But to stand at the mouth of a mountain with a dead tree behind you and a cursed one ahead, with a mage hunter at your elbow who has waited a hundred years for someone to finish her clan's work, and to say not yet, we are going home for potions first: that takes a kind of courage the bards never sing about, because it does not scan.

This company has it. I have come to believe it is the rarest thing about them.

I. The Parting at the Halls

The Seething Halls lie forty miles south of Port Nyanzaru, in the jungle between the Soshenstar and the Tiryki, where the trees stand so close that noon comes through them green and the mouth of a temple can be ten paces off and unseen. The morning mist hangs among the trunks so thick and so white that a man standing at the cave mouth that serves for the temple's door seems to be standing at the bottom of a drowned world. On the nineteenth of Uktar, in that white silence, Xhosala Obanashi stood at that door with her hunters at her back and listened to five outlanders tell her they were leaving.

Understand what she is. The Obanashi were the mage hunters of old Chult, the order that kept the Heart of the Wild beating in this very mountain until the Spellplague came and a Nimbrese wizard named Kolate talked their high priestess out of her secret and walked off with a god's breath in a coin. Xhosala is what is left of that order, and she wears a century's worth of her clan's failure the way other women wear jewelry. She had not come to this door to be told to wait.

Yet wait she did. The company laid it out for her as soldiers lay out a campaign: fifty miles of blighted jungle south to the Forsaken Tree, a root-maze beneath it where no rest would be possible, and five adventurers with their potion satchels nearly empty and their guide unpaid since midsummer. She looked from one to the next, the gold dragonborn who carried himself like a lord, the wulven with his trident, the little gnome whose eyes gave away nothing, the goblin with a rune-lit rod at his belt, the tabaxi who had not stopped watching the treeline the whole time anyone spoke, and whatever she saw there, she gave way to it. Her people would hold the Halls. Now that the spirit naga was so much carrion in the Hall of the Rising Sun, there was a temple to be cleared and reconsecrated, and the Obanashi had waited a hundred years to begin.

So the companies divided at the cave mouth, Xhosala's hunters turning back into the dark of the door, and the five going out into the white mist and the trees, with Artus Cimber and the saurial Dragonbait beside them, and Shago the guide carrying his spear as he has carried it since Fort Beluarian, and one more: the tall, dark, green-eyed woman in the old Mezroan style who called herself Nerissa, and who would be the matter of this whole chapter without ever once lifting a blade.

II. The Road East

It is forty miles from the Seething Halls north to Port Nyanzaru, as the pteranodon flies, and considerably more as the adventurer stumbles, for the country between the rivers is jungle of the thickest sort and the rivers themselves are in no hurry to let anyone past. I have made the crossing of the northern jungle myself (Volo's Guide to the Lands of Intrigue, revised edition, available wherever books of quality are sold) and I will say only that the trees are the least of it. It is the water that gets you: the water that falls, the water that rises out of the ground, the water in the air that soaks the sweat off your back before your back has finished making it.

The company met it with arithmetic. They divided the day into three parts of eight hours apiece: eight for the march, all of them together under the dripping green; eight in which half the company slept beneath a dome of force while the other half kept watch; and eight more in which the watchers slept and the sleepers watched. It is a soldier's device, and a good one, and it says something about how this company has changed since I first set eyes on them in Port Nyanzaru that nobody had to argue them into it.

The watches fell out thus. In the one: Artus Cimber, Dragonbait, Vex, and Chumble Crudluck. In the other: Nerissa, Shago, Urida, Grieg, and Lilac Mist. Mark the arrangement. It was not an accident, and it put the woman from Mezro among those who had the keenest noses and the lightest fingers in the company, with a hut's width between her and the one man who might have objected.

On the first night out from the Halls, with the forest ticking and dripping around them and the hut's pale shell glowing faintly against the dark, Artus Cimber sat with Vex and the goblin and unburdened himself. He did it quietly, by the goblin's own account. He did it like a man who has carried something a long way and is tired of the weight.

Dragonbait, he told them, has a sense for the inside of people. Saurials speak in scents, as any scholar of the Lost Vale will tell you (I have written on the subject at length, and been quoted without credit more than once), and when the dragon-man turned his snout toward Nerissa, what came off him was lemons and honeysuckle: nothing rotten, nothing false, but nothing simple either. Artus had been talking to her on the road. She knew Mezro. Not as a traveler knows a city, from the gates and the market, but as a daughter knows a house: the names of buildings, the turn of particular streets, faces she had passed in them. She knew the Hall of Champions in the great temple of Ubtao, and the statues that stood in it. There is no book in which that is written. One does not learn it. One is simply from there.

And so he had asked her, because he could not help himself. He asked whether she had known Alisanda.

I must pause on that name, for those who do not know it. Alisanda is Artus Cimber's wife. He met her in Mezro, and she was in Mezro when the city went wherever it has gone, and the world presumed her lost with it. Artus has never presumed any such thing. He has told this company plainly that she is there still, and that Mezro is not where the map puts it. Everything he has done in Chult, every mile he has walked under the Ring of Winter's cold weight, has been toward her.

He told Vex and Chumble that there had been something in Nerissa's eyes when he said it. A flicker, as if the name had reached something in her that she could not reach herself. And then it was gone, and she told him only that the name was vaguely familiar, and that she could not say.

Her mind, he said, is broken. Not mad, broken: the way a dropped pot is broken, every piece present and none of them in place. He does not believe she knows her own name. He suspects Nerissa is a cover thrown over the hole where a name should be. Her insistence that every vision is a message from Ubtao he took for the one thing rooted deep enough to survive the breaking: she had been devout, and devotion was what came back first. And here Artus said a thing that the dragonborn marked and kept, for Vex misses very little that touches on a man's standing with his gods: he did not himself always agree with Ubtao. He did not think the Father of Dinosaurs' way of seeing the world was the only one, or the best.

Then he came to the point. When this company goes down into Omu after Ras Nsi, Nerissa will want to follow. He asked them not to allow it. She is the last living thread he has found that leads to Mezro, and if the five of them are fated to die in the dark under that cursed city, then so be it, but she must not die with them.

It was a great deal to put on a goblin and a dragonborn on the first night of a five-day march. They took it. I have noticed that about these two; they are the ones who take things.

III. What Was in the Pack

That same night, the woman who called herself Nerissa could not sleep.

She lay a while in the hut among the others, and rose, and went out into the wet dark to breathe, the way people do who are running from something behind their own eyes. The dome closed behind her. And Lilac Mist and Urida, who were awake and on watch and had been listening to her breathe for an hour, looked at one another, and at the pack she had left beside her bedroll, and did not need to say anything at all.

I am a chronicler, not a magistrate. I record what was done. Lilac Mist went to the pack without a sound. Urida went with a wizard's thoroughness. The ranger searched. The gnome found.

There was, first, a ticket. A wager ticket, printed in the port, for the dinosaur races that run through Port Nyanzaru's streets every tenday to the ruin of a great many purses, mine among them on more than one occasion. A small thing. A human thing, and strange to find in the pack of a woman who claimed to have woken ten days ago in a flooded city a century out of time.

There was, second, a hidden sleeve sewn into the lining, and in it a journal.

Urida leafed through it fast, by the light that comes through a tiny hut's walls, which is to say by nearly none. It was about the Death Curse. That much she caught: pages of a hand that was not a warrior's hand, tracing the curse through the city. And as she turned the pages a loose sheet slid out of the back and fell into her lap, and she made a decision that I would have made and that most honest folk would not: she put the journal back exactly as it had been, and kept the letter.

It was addressed from someone called Wren to someone called Mesika.

A wax seal had once closed it, and the better part of the seal had crumbled away, but what remained showed a crescent moon, and beside it the left side of something curved, as though the moon were cradling the edge of a thing one could not quite make out. The hand inside was a sprawling, cheerful, slightly sideways hand, the hand of a man writing after dinner and some way into the evening. The cursed thingamawhatsit, Wren wrote, was not connected to the bleedin' curse that had been sucking all the fun out of the city. Who knew what it was really for; the society folk did not seem to know for certain, but thought those party-pooper yuan-ti might have been aiming at someone high up the chain. Either way, Kaya was still helping him forget as much of it as possible.

Three things happened to that letter in the next quarter hour, and each of them was done by a different member of the company, and I set them down because together they are as neat a piece of detective work as has ever been recounted to me outside a Waterdeep magistrate's hall.

Grieg, who had been asleep, was not any longer, and when the letter passed under his nose his nose did what a wulven's nose does. There was drink on the paper. Not the smell of a tavern, which clings to everything in Chult, but the particular ghost of good spirits spilled near a good pen. And Grieg, who has a hunter's memory for a scent once met, remembered a name he had heard in the port: Kaya, of Kaya's House of Repose, in the Market Ward. The letter had been written in an inn. He could tell them which.

Then they fetched Vex from his watch, because Vex is a noble of Waterdeep and a cousin to Azlund, and had spent his youth in rooms where certain quiet people came and went. He looked at the broken seal and knew it. The crescent moon with the harp's curve beside it: the mark of the Harpers, those spellcasters and spies who oppose the abuse of power everywhere in Faerûn and admit to it nowhere. He had seen it around his cousin's business more than once.

So, in the space of a watch, in a hut in the jungle: a Harper named Wren, writing from an inn in Port Nyanzaru, to a woman he called Mesika, about a cursed thing that was not the Death Curse and yuan-ti who had been aiming at someone important. And the woman who carried that letter in a hidden sleeve was outside in the rain telling herself she was Nerissa.

She came back in. She had heard something, a shuffle, a whisper, and she came in through the dome with a soldier's quickness and looked round at the company, and whatever she saw did not trouble her. She lay down. In a little while she slept, truly slept, the way the exhausted do.

And Lilac Mist went back to the pack.

This time she took the journal, and read it properly, with a ranger's patience, over the sleeping woman's own shoulder. The first entry was dated twenty-seven days before. The last was ten days old. It was the diary of an investigator: someone tracking the Death Curse through Port Nyanzaru with care and method, and with the dry, unhurried intelligence of a person who had done this kind of work before.

And it was wrong. Not in its facts: in its shape. There were places where the writer set down a discovery, a revelation, a thing learned and understood, and then, pages on and days later, set down the same discovery again, fresh, as if for the first time. Twice over. The hand was the same. The surprise was the same. Whoever wrote that journal had been learning the same things again and again, and each time believed it was the first.

Ten days ago, she had told them, the fire of every color came down on her. Ten days ago the journal stopped.
